correctness.rationale: In the finite poset representation H = Up(P), the pseudocomplement of U is P minus the down-closure of U. Thus excluded middle holds exactly when U is both an upset and a downset, i.e. a union of comparability components. With r components and n_i upsets on component i, there are 2^r excluded-middle elements out of product n_i. The nontriviality assumption ensures r ≥ 1 and n_i ≥ 2; disjoint unions of chains on n_i−1 points realize all lists of n_i. If product n_i = 2^s q and the reduced numerator is 2^a > 1, then a=r−s and Ω(q)+s≥r, since each factor contributes at least one prime. Conversely partition the odd denominator's prime factors into a nonempty groups to construct the requisite chain sizes. One chain of size 2q realizes every 1/q, including 1. This proves the claimed spectrum and verifies the positive and negative examples without a finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: No finite script replay or formal certification; neither is needed for the symbolic argument.
